body.statement: For a polynomial \(D\) satisfying Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}d\text{-}nonzero\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}d\text{-}nonconstant\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}d\text{-}homogeneous\), the identity \(2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_D(X)X)^2\}=cD(X)^2\) holds on \(S3\) if and only if there exist \(V1\subset V2\), \(a,b,e\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) with \(a+b+e>0\), and \(\lambda_0\neq0\) such that \(D=D_{\mathrm{flag}}\). In that representation, \(c=2\{(a+b+e)^2+(b+e)^2+e^2\}\), and every active flag subspace is unique.
body.justification: This degree-unrestricted converse is the algebraic engine for a complete audit of reduced three-variable rational causal denominators.
body.gap: Tamano's Theorem 1 proves flag sufficiency, while Theorem 3 supplies determinant stripping, spectral reduction, and the pure branches; Theorem 3 and Remark 4 leave the mixed kernel line open, and Lemma 3 together with Theorem 2 closes exactly that branch.
body.consumer: Proposition 6 turns the classification into an iff audit for reduced half-trek and other rational covariance certificates.
body.proof_tex:
Assume first the self-normalization identity with \(c>0\).  The three algebraic assumptions place \(D\) in \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{SN},3}\).  Apply the cited Tamano three-dimensional reduction after writing \(D=\delta^eE\) with maximal \(e\).  Its constant, line, and plane branches already have respectively the forms \(\lambda_0\delta^e\), \(\lambda_0\Delta_1^a\delta^e\), and \(\lambda_0\Delta_2^b\delta^e\), with the unused member of the flag chosen arbitrarily so as to obtain \(V1\subset V2\).

It remains to treat the mixed branch.  The cited reduction supplies integers \(a,b\geq1\), interior nonvanishing, and
\[
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\frac{G_E(X)X}{E(X)}\right)=\{a+b,b,0\}
 \qquad(X\in C3). \tag{9}
\]
The mixed-residue bridge shows that the signed residue \(F=sE\) is homogeneous and that \(G_F\) is positive semidefinite of rank two on \(C3\), with \(\det G_F\equiv0\).  The positive-gradient kernel-rigidity theorem therefore provides a fixed \(u\neq0\) with \(G_F(X)u=0\) identically.  After an orthogonal change of coordinates taking \(u\) to the third coordinate direction, \(F\) is a polynomial \(f\) of the leading \(2\times2\) symmetric compression.

For a positive-definite \(2\times2\) matrix \(Y\), insert \(X=\operatorname{diag}(Y,z)\) with \(z>0\).  Because \(G_FX/F\) has the spectrum in (9),
\[
 2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_F(X)X)^2\}
 =2\bigl((a+b)^2+b^2\bigr)F(X)^2
\]
on \(C3\), and hence identically by polynomial continuation.  The zero third row and column of \(G_F(X)\) now show that \(f\) satisfies the corresponding two-dimensional exact self-normalization identity.  The cited two-dimensional converse then gives
\[
 f(Y)=\lambda_0\det(CYC^{\top})^a\det(Y)^b
\]
for a nonzero row vector \(C\), after relabeling its line exponent and determinant exponent.  These exponents are indeed the same \(a,b\) as in (9), because the ordered relative eigenvalues of this two-dimensional flag power are \(a+b,b\).  Returning to the original coordinates identifies \(V2=u^{\perp}\) and a line \(V1\subset V2\), and restoring the stripped determinant gives
\[
 D(X)=\lambda_0\Delta_1(X)^a\Delta_2(X)^b\delta(X)^e.
\]

Conversely, the cited flag-sufficiency theorem applies to every such nested flag form and gives
\[
 2\operatorname{tr}\{(G_D(X)X)^2\}
 =2\bigl((a+b+e)^2+(b+e)^2+e^2\bigr)D(X)^2. \tag{10}
\]
The positive sum condition makes \(D\) nonconstant, and the displayed constant is positive.  Since \(D^2\not\equiv0\), comparison with the assumed identity also shows that the value of \(c\) is forced to be the value in (10).

For completeness, active-flag uniqueness is algebraic.  The coordinate ring of \(S3\) is a unique-factorization domain.  After an invertible congruence change of variables, a line minor is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(x_{11}\), a plane minor is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(x_{11}x_{22}-x_{12}^2\), and the full determinant is \(\delta\).  The first two are irreducible.  To see irreducibility of \(\delta\), regard it as a degree-one polynomial in \(x_{33}\).  A proper factor independent of \(x_{33}\) would divide both its coefficient \(x_{11}x_{22}-x_{12}^2\) and its constant term, but the irreducible coefficient does not divide that constant term, as is seen on the specialization \(x_{11}=1,x_{12}=x_{22}=0\).  Thus \(\delta\) is irreducible as well.  Unique factorization identifies every active factor up to a nonzero scalar.  Associate line minors have proportional rank-one coefficient matrices and hence the same line.  Writing a plane minor, up to a nonzero scalar, as \(v^{\top}\operatorname{adj}(X)v\), associate plane minors have proportional matrices \(vv^{\top}\) and hence the same orthogonal-complement line, so they determine the same plane.  Therefore every subspace whose exponent is positive is unique; an inactive subspace is, correctly, not asserted to be unique.
